items.note: The plan gives h, v, N, m, the I=3v^2 invocations with their own scratch wires, and the eight-row schedule. It derives the net change (JV+RG)x independently of a,c, with the bit coefficient |S∩T| mod 2 and the complex coefficient (|S∩T|-1)/2, and composes forward, inverse and forward into (x,y)->(-y,x). It also gives the neighbour and wire counts, all matching 741-783. The gather and scatter maps are not written out, but their coefficients are.

The plan states that the gate frame is shared, that the edge change is D_vD_u^{-1}, that the invariant holds by induction and that a common frame commutes with the pointwise gate. It reaches D_out S D_in^{-1} and the route operator eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}, following 804-825.

The plan covers the bilinear forms, the terminal labels, the stage transitions, the full gate-label table, every row of the residual table, the single decrease at center 3->4, L=Ich, Wm-2N+2L and both loss ratios, all faithful to 856-1071. It omits the lemma's last clause and its proof (1008-1009, 1073-1102): every nonzero binary residual is nonalternating and so has an orthonormal basis. That argument is in the item's derivation range, and the complex kernel count relies on it.

The plan states P_U at gates and sinks and -P_{U_a} at the sources X_a. It derives rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, the N exceptional first edges 2P_{U_a} of rank one, and the endpoint identity P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m. It reaches s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m, as in 1156-1172. The frame Phi_M and the shear on every role appear in S0.1.1.2.1.

The plan follows 1231-1310 in order. Weight is additive mod 4 on orthogonal vectors; odd weight gives a sign; Hadamard conjugation turns the phase into a translation kernel. The count is s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c. The zero and full labels give I and C^{⊗m}. The X_a->Y_a pair has C^{-1} on 27 coordinates, fixed by Z wrappers and i^{27k}. The final negation of the X outputs and the undoing of the exchange (1311-1314) are not spelled out, and the existence of orthonormal bases is assumed rather than cited.

The plan gives L/N=100/539 and 101/539 (<1/2), s_b<W_b m and s_c<W_c m (deficit 2N-2L_c), and the exact eta_b and eta_c. It derives m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20*2^{-50})>m(1-eta) from log m<20, so s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, exactly as in 1331-1344.

The plan names the stream lemmas only as 'relies on: elementary-stream-ops, controlled-shift' and applies them: linear-time triangular updates, cyclic row splitting, single-bit moves and prefix-controlled shifts. It never states the lemmas' content, such as the list of O(V) digit operations or the controlled update y->y+a(controls) mod q^b with b^{O(1)} offset preparation.

The plan states the factorization A=E_1 Pi E_2 with the topmost-row, rightmost-entry elimination and the specialization modulo a fixed odd prime. Triangular factors cost O(V) when updated in descending order. Each one of Pi is realized as D_j+=H_i, a swap, then D_j=H_i-D_j, one interchange each. This follows 1375-1447; the condition that q also avoid diagonal numerators is left out.

The plan covers the contract eq:finite-shear-contract, the cyclic split into W role streams of volume V/W, Phi_{A_e} per edge done recursively, Phi_{I_m} on every role, the merge, and the three shears. It derives the s calls, F_0=O(1), F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), the geometric-sum case split and F_k=O(e^tau), plus the fixed-tape parking stack, all as in 1491-1588.

Every step of 1649-1762 is reproduced: rho high digits as the row field with q^{2rho}>=W^k, the field-order sequence, zero-row padding to R'<2R, base-m pieces summing to O(Ve^tau), padding binary ranges to [q^e] at a fixed factor, and the one-bit-difference case.

The plan states the C identities, the edge product over a residual basis, and the conjugation P_M X_v P_M^{-1}=X_{Mv}. It gives the slot and column layout, one child per kernel, (C^{-1})^{⊗f}=(-i)^f Z C Z, at most m(m-1)+3m row additions, exactly s_c children on f=e/m axes, and H_0^{⊗D}=b^D S_D C^{⊗D} S_D. All of this matches 1835-1931.

The plan covers the eight operations and their two 3-cycles composing to the parity flip with w restored. It gives the guard segments, each line as one cyclic shift, the bad set from the guard interval [10,2^{K-1}-11] with |B|<=delta_bad M, T_0S_0^{-1} permuting B, the radix-sort repair, the omitted top bit and the full time bound. This matches 2013-2226.

The plan derives the node overhead O(V((eK)^tau+1)) and the q_0 rows padded to a multiple of W^{k_0}, with children of volume exactly V/W. It gives F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) with leaves O(e), K<=e^{c/beta}, internal sum O(e^lambda), leaf sum O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}), and the base-m pieces giving O(d^{lambda'}). This follows 2286-2445.

The plan states that the layer returns Q_p(Hz) in O(Vd^{lambda'}) with error <sqrt2 2^{-p}, and derives the guard width: E, B, nu, C_1, C_0, A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E, the bound 8B^2 d^{nu+1}, the total <C_0 d^{C_1}, and Delta=o(p) from eps C_1<1. It adds the row-sum-one truncation argument, following 2457-2584 and 2686-2758. The check that the packed lemma's cost is uniform over the parameter bands (2696-2735) is only implicit.

The plan derives character cancellation through the shift argument and the absence of two-torsion. It gives decimation in frequency with bit-reversed storage B_t, the reverse procedure giving F_t^+B_t^{-1}, and the grouped round. For the layout it gives the prefix slots, at most Dq-1 chunk exchanges costing O(Tp pK^{tau-1}), the fast rounds, the prefix rounds, and the commutation J_E Q_p=Q_p J_E with the error count, as in 2819-3199.

The plan gives B_0=2^{4p}, four products by the established multiplier, the separation |h_j|<=r2^{2p}<B_0/2, both carry recurrences with their carry ranges, centered extraction, reduction mod y^r+1, and the O(rp log(rp)) cost. This follows 3233-3367.

The plan gives M_r=(f*g)/T as a bilinear contraction, the retained LB order with P(LBu,LBv)=LB P(u,v), and F^-(f*g)=M F^-f F^-g. It derives the error chain 2delta+eta, then 3delta+eta, then M(3delta+eta)=sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^{-p}, and the cost, as in 3414-3494.

The plan follows the paper's route: the Gaussian identity, N=CTD with ||N-I||<1/2 by Neumann series, and the rescalings S', J', D' with norms 3/4, 7/8, 1. The left inverse gives 2^{-2alpha^2}P_sF_s, followed by the error and time table, C as an ordered selection and the unexecuted sorts. It then tensors with gamma=2d alpha^2, with line costs and axis exposure in O(Tp d^2(1+l^tau)).

Both identities and their proofs follow 3938-3983: chirp periodicity and the kernel computation, then F^+R_c=R_c^{-1}F^+, RF^+R=F^+, and the normalizations giving (u*v)/S^2. The lemma's last clause is missing everywhere in the plan: an algorithm for RF_s^+ comes from complex conjugation of input and output (3934-3935, 3983-3987).

The plan gives all the fixed rationals, the sizes b, p, d, K, T, r and t_i with their Theta-relations and comparison constants, and alpha and gamma. It derives the prime existence from Rosser-Schoenfeld, the disjoint intervals, T/2<S<T by Bernoulli, alpha^4 theta_i>p, the n^{o(1)} search and the no-wraparound digit bound, all matching 4007-4193.

The plan gives mu_i, the isomorphism from the order of the image of x, the triangular formula b_i with its justification, the update order i=d..1, preservation of the padding, prefix-controlled shifts, O(d^2) axis moves and the O(Tp d^2(1+l^tau)) cost, as in 4204-4292.

The plan shows Theta is well defined via (zeta y)^r=1, diagonal with factor zeta^k, an isometric isomorphism, and that the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j holds. It gives M_C=D_-iota^{-1}M_r(iota D_+f, iota D_+g)=(f*g)/T, the computed twist sequence, and twist errors below 4 each in the error chain.

The plan gives the chirp transform, the source transform with exact counterpart 2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A=RF_s, the digit input scaled by 2^{-b-2}, the six steps, and the explanation of the two factors of S, all faithful to 4486-4544. It never defines the opposite procedure F~^+(z)=conj(F~(conj z)) (4478-4484), which step 4 uses.

The plan follows the full error chain: E_ring<5TL, then <6TL, <8TL, E_s=9*2^gamma TL, 2E_s+2, 3E_s+2 and E_w<28*2^gamma T^2 L. The final bound is <448b 2^{-3b/4}<1/2 using S<=T<2^b, L<b and gamma<=b/4, followed by rounding and the carry recurrence with its invariant, as in 4557-4805.

The plan covers all seven table rows with their powers and margins g_1..g_7, min g_i=2^{-181}=2kappa, and the justification of each row. It then gives setup o(Tp), the powers at most 1-2kappa with log factors at most p^kappa, O(n(log n)^{1-kappa}), and the schoolbook cutoff, matching 4815-4995. The bound on exceptional sorting streams (4951-4973) is not stated separately.

S0 says only 'disproving the n log n optimality conjecture'. It never states what an eventual lower bound means (T_A(n)>=c_A n lg n for every machine), that its negation needs liminf T_A(n)/(n lg n)=0 for one machine, or that the power saving gives limit zero.

errors.says: Motivation: subspace labels let adjacent vertices be nested, so the deficit Wm-s 'equals twice the total number of loss minus source ranks'.
errors.paper: The deficit is N-2L_b for the bit network and 2N-2L_c for the complex one: source ranks minus twice the loss, not twice the loss minus source ranks.

errors.says: The labels are built from triple indicators 'pairing as |σ∩σ'|-1', stated for both networks.
errors.paper: The pairing |S∩T|-1 belongs to the rational form x^T(I-J/9)y of the bit network. The complex network uses F_2^h with the ordinary dot product, where t_T·t_T=1. S0.1.1.1.4.1 later corrects this.

errors.says: The side-wire edge 0->2 gains a residual of dimension (a-1)(h-1)+1 'using that the two triples are orthogonal'.
errors.paper: The residual of 0->2 is (B⊗t_Y^perp)⊥(P⊗<t_X>) and follows directly from the splittings. The paper names the side edge 2->5 as the one that uses the neighbour relation t_X⊥t_Y essentially.

errors.says: The recurrence 'solves to a cost O(e^tau) ... for the bit network and O(e^lambda) in the complex one'.
errors.paper: For the complex network the internal cost is O(e^lambda) but the leaves add O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}), which depends on d. Only after summing the base-m pieces is the total O(d^{lambda'}). S0.1.1.1.6.2 states this correctly.

errors.says: 'per-node overheads are polynomial in p and absorbed by the length of the polynomial record'.
errors.paper: The node overhead is O(V((eK)^tau+1)) from basis changes, gates and corrections, and it enters the recurrence. Only descriptor and address work polynomial in p per record is absorbed by the record length.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route to the main bound. It runs from the scalar bank-exchange network, frames and nested labels to the two interfaces and the exponent tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}. From there it runs through the rank-a shear, the interchange recurrence, arbitrary-width swaps, phase-frame children, packed selected-bit additions and the layer recurrence, then synthetic transforms, ring convolution, resampling, chirp, CRT and twist, the six-step algorithm, exact recovery and the cost table with min margin 2kappa. It thins in a few places. The stream primitives are only named. The F_2 orthonormal-basis existence behind the complex kernel count is never established. The conjugation that defines the opposite source transform is missing. The disproof of the conjecture is asserted rather than argued.

steps.note: The plan gives h=100, N=v^3 and m=h^3 with banks indexed by triples, the eight-row schedule with scratch cancellation, and forward, inverse and forward stages giving (x,y)->(-y,x) while restoring every scratch wire.
The plan states that a shared frame commutes with the pointwise gate, so the network implements D_out S D_in^{-1}. Each edge pays only D_vD_u^{-1}, and endpoint frames fix the route operator.

The plan gives nondegenerate labels in F^{⊗3} of dimension m, the full gate-label table, comparable labels on every edge, and the central 3->4 edges as the only decrease, each losing P⊗F of dimension h.
The plan states rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U for nested U⊂V, unchanged under reversal, and identifies the N first source edges 2P_{U_a} as the rank-one exceptions.
Sources total N and sinks Wm-N, so the signed changes sum to Wm-2N, and absolute changes add 2L with L=Ich. Adding the N source ranks gives s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.

The plan gives L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539 <1/2, hence s_b<W_b m and s_c<W_c m with deficit 2N-2L_c. The bit deficit N-2L_b follows from the stated formulas, but the motivation of S0.1.1.1.4 garbles it.

The plan gives the endpoint difference P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m, with zero source and identity sink on the other roles. Hence Phi_{M_out}Phi_{-M_in}=Phi_{I_m} gives H<-H+D on every role, scratch rows included, and the merge undoes rho.
The plan factors A=E_1 Pi E_2 with O(V) triangular parts and one interchange per one of Pi, so an edge of rank a costs a recursive interchanges. The node makes exactly s calls.

The plan gives children of volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), and tau=1-2^{-50} from eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20 giving s/W<m^tau. It solves the geometric sum with the a<=1 and a>1 cases to F_k=O(e^tau).

central.summary: All nine steps of the central saving are reconstructed with their defining content, in the paper's order and roles: the network, frames, labels, rank equal to dimension change, the budget, the strict saving, the endpoint identity, the shear cost and the recurrence with tau=1-2^{-50}. The only blemish is a garbled sign in one motivation line (the deficit described as twice the loss minus the source ranks); the plan's own formulas get it right.
